def probe_workload(
    static_set: StaticSet,
    *,
    namespace: str,
    generation: int,
) -> tuple[Literal["ReplicaSet", "DaemonSet"], dict[str, Any]]:
    """Build the scheduling probe for one StaticSet generation.

    Args:
        static_set: The owning StaticSet.
        namespace: The namespace to create the probe in.
        generation: The StaticSet generation the probe is created for.

    Returns:
        The workload's kind and its complete manifest.
    """
    spec = static_set.spec
    name = static_set.metadata.name or ""
    labels = probe_labels(static_set.metadata.uid or "", name, generation)
    template = probe_pod_template(static_set, generation=generation)
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": probe_workload_name(name, generation),
        "namespace": namespace,
        "labels": {**labels, "app.kubernetes.io/managed-by": MANAGED_BY},
        "annotations": {
            ANNOTATION_SET: name,
            ANNOTATION_SET_UID: static_set.metadata.uid or "",
            ANNOTATION_GENERATION: str(generation),
        },
    }
    owner = _owner_reference(static_set)
    if owner:
        metadata["ownerReferences"] = owner
    workload_spec: dict[str, Any] = {
        "selector": {"matchLabels": labels},
        "template": template,
    }
    if spec.mode is Mode.DEPLOYMENT:
        workload_spec["replicas"] = spec.replicas
        kind: Literal["ReplicaSet", "DaemonSet"] = "ReplicaSet"
    else:
        # ``OnDelete`` so the DaemonSet controller never replaces a probe Pod on its
        # own: a probe exists for one generation and is deleted as a whole, and a
        # controller-initiated replacement would silently re-run a scheduling pass
        # the operator believes is finished.
        workload_spec["updateStrategy"] = {"type": "OnDelete"}
        kind = "DaemonSet"
    return kind, {
        "apiVersion": "apps/v1",
        "kind": kind,
        "metadata": metadata,
        "spec": workload_spec,
    }

docs.title: revision
docs.text:
Deterministic revision identity for a compiled static workload.

A revision names a content: the compiled static Pod plus every configuration file it needs. Two compilations of the same inputs must produce the same revision, and any change to a ConfigMap, a Secret, a field of the template or a policy that affects the emitted manifest must produce a different one. Nothing that varies per node, per installer or per wall-clock time may enter the hash, or a rollout would never converge.

def compute_revision(
    pod: Mapping[str, Any],
    files: Mapping[str, bytes],
    modes: Mapping[str, int],
) -> str:
    """Return the deterministic revision of a compiled workload.

    Args:
        pod: The compiled static Pod with *relative* configuration mount paths, so
            that the hash cannot depend on where the bundle happens to be mounted.
        files: Configuration files by bundle-relative path.
        modes: The file mode of each path in ``files``.

    Returns:
        The revision token.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``modes`` names a path that is not in ``files``.
    """
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    digest.update(_canonical(pod))
    for path in sorted(files):
        content = files[path]
        mode = modes[path]
        digest.update(b"\x00")
        digest.update(path.encode("utf-8"))
        digest.update(b"\x00")
        digest.update(f"{mode:o}".encode("ascii"))
        digest.update(b"\x00")
        digest.update(hashlib.sha256(content).digest())
    return f"{REVISION_PREFIX}{digest.hexdigest()[:32]}"

docs.title: translation
docs.text:
Compile a supported PodTemplateSpec into a self-contained static Pod.

The compiler never guesses. Every ConfigMap and Secret the template references is resolved now, its data is materialized into revision-specific files, and the emitted Pod mounts those files read-only. What cannot be resolved without the API server is rejected with a message that names the field and the supported alternative, because a static Pod that silently lost a field would start, look healthy, and behave differently from the template it was compiled from.

What the emitted Pod does not carry is as important as what it does:

  • no scheduler placement (nodeSelector, affinity, tolerations, topologySpreadConstraints) — kubelet never schedules a static Pod, so those fields would be inert; they belong to spec.placement;
  • no serviceAccountName, imagePullSecrets or projected service-account token — all of them need the API server, which is precisely what a reboot must not need;
  • no hostPath volume taken from the template — the only hostPath mounts in the manifest are the revision directories this compiler materialized, which keeps the workload inside the bundle the installer owns.

Secret material is handled deliberately. A ConfigMap value is not confidential, so it is inlined into the environment where the template asked for it. A Secret value is written to a mode-restricted file inside the revision directory, and a Secret asked for as a literal environment value is refused unless the StaticSet opts in (spec.policy.allowInlineSecretEnv), because the only offline ways to satisfy that request both disclose the value: either it is written into the manifest — and therefore into the mirror Pod and into every copy of the manifest — or the variable is simply gone after the reboot.

def compile_workload(spec: StaticSetSpec, resolved: ResolvedConfig) -> CompiledWorkload:
    """Compile a StaticSet specification into a self-contained static Pod.

    Args:
        spec: The validated specification.
        resolved: The configuration the template's references were resolved to.

    Returns:
        The compiled workload, including its deterministic revision.

    Raises:
        UnsupportedFieldError: If the template uses a field or a policy
            combination this operator does not support.
        SecretDisclosureError: If Secret material would have to be disclosed.
        TranslationError: If a referenced ConfigMap or Secret is missing and not
            optional.
    """
    pod_spec = spec.template.spec
    check_policies(spec)

    materializer = _Materializer(resolved)
    volumes = _build_volumes(pod_spec, materializer)

    containers = [
        _compile_container(item, pod_spec, spec, materializer) for item in pod_spec.containers
    ]
    init_containers = [
        _compile_container(item, pod_spec, spec, materializer)
        for item in pod_spec.init_containers or []
    ]

    pod = _assemble_pod(spec, containers, init_containers, volumes)
    revision = compute_revision(pod, materializer.files, materializer.modes)
    return CompiledWorkload(
        pod=pod,
        files=materializer.files,
        modes=materializer.modes,
        references=tuple(sorted(materializer.references)),
        revision=revision,

def config_references(spec: StaticSetSpec) -> tuple[ConfigReference, ...]:
    """Return every ConfigMap and Secret a template names, before resolving them.

    The installer needs the names *before* it can read the objects, and the
    controller needs them to decide which changes require a new revision.

    Args:
        spec: The validated specification.

    Returns:
        The references, sorted and deduplicated.
    """
    pod_spec = spec.template.spec
    references: set[ConfigReference] = set()
    for volume in pod_spec.volumes or []:
        if volume.config_map is not None:
            references.add(ConfigReference("ConfigMap", volume.config_map.name))
        if volume.secret is not None:
            references.add(ConfigReference("Secret", volume.secret.secret_name))
    for container in [*pod_spec.containers, *(pod_spec.init_containers or [])]:
        for env_var in container.env or []:
            source = env_var.value_from
            if source is None:
                continue
            if source.config_map_key_ref is not None:
                references.add(ConfigReference("ConfigMap", source.config_map_key_ref.name))
            if source.secret_key_ref is not None:
                references.add(ConfigReference("Secret", source.secret_key_ref.name))
        for env_from in container.env_from or []:
            if env_from.config_map_ref is not None:
                references.add(ConfigReference("ConfigMap", env_from.config_map_ref.name))
            if env_from.secret_ref is not None:
                references.add(ConfigReference("Secret", env_from.secret_ref.name))
    return tuple(sorted(references))

def referenced_config(resolved: ResolvedConfig) -> tuple[ConfigReference, ...]:
    """Return the references implied by a resolved configuration set.

    Args:
        resolved: The configuration read from the cluster.

    Returns:
        The ConfigMap and Secret references, sorted and deduplicated.
    """
    references = {ConfigReference("ConfigMap", name) for name in resolved.config_maps}
    references |= {ConfigReference("Secret", name) for name in resolved.secrets}
    return tuple(sorted(references))

def render_manifest(
    compiled: CompiledWorkload,
    *,
    pod_name: str,
    namespace: str,
    revision_dir: str,
    labels: Mapping[str, str],
    annotations: Mapping[str, str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Render the final static Pod manifest for one placement.

    The only per-placement inputs are the Pod's name, its namespace, the directory
    the materialized files live in and the provenance labels and annotations.
    Nothing here can change the revision, so the same compiled content renders the
    same revision on every node.

    Args:
        compiled: The compiled workload.
        pod_name: The static Pod's name, which kubelet also needs as file name.
        namespace: The namespace the mirror Pod should appear in.
        revision_dir: The absolute directory holding this revision's files.
        labels: Provenance labels to merge onto the static Pod.
        annotations: Provenance annotations to merge onto the static Pod.

    Returns:
        The complete static Pod manifest.
    """
    pod = copy.deepcopy(compiled.pod)
    metadata = pod.setdefault("metadata", {})
    metadata["name"] = pod_name
    metadata["namespace"] = namespace
    metadata["labels"] = {**metadata.get("labels", {}), **labels}
    metadata["annotations"] = {**metadata.get("annotations", {}), **annotations}
    for volume in pod.get("spec", {}).get("volumes", []):
        host_path = volume.get("hostPath")
        if host_path is not None:
            host_path["path"] = f"{revision_dir.rstrip('/')}/{host_path['path']}"
    return pod

docs.title: validation
docs.text:
Strict admission validation for a StaticSet.

The generated CustomResourceDefinition is a structural schema, so the API server prunes a field it does not know instead of refusing it. A pruned field means a template that asked for something the operator cannot compile would be accepted and then silently ignored — the one outcome the translation layer exists to prevent.

This module turns the same model validation into a list of actionable problems, so the operator can refuse such an object at admission instead of pruning it. It is wired to a validating admission webhook in the operator entry point; without that webhook the CRD-level pruning still applies, which is why the installation guide tells you to deploy with --webhook.

def strict_problems(body: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Return the reasons a StaticSet body must be refused.

    Every problem names the exact field path, so the message can be attached to the
    rejection the user sees from ``kubectl``.

    Args:
        body: The raw object as the API server received it.

    Returns:
        The problems, in field order. An empty list means the object is acceptable.
    """
    try:
        resource = StaticSet.model_validate(body)
    except ValidationError as error:
        return _describe(error)
    try:
        check_policies(resource.spec)
    except StaticSetsError as error:
        return [f"spec: {error}"]
    return []

docs.title: workload
docs.text:
The supported subset of a workload PodTemplateSpec.

Only the fields this operator can compile into a self-contained static Pod are modelled. A field that is not modelled is not silently ignored: because every model forbids unknown fields, it is rejected while the object is validated, and the operator refuses to install a workload it would otherwise quietly degrade.

Two groups of fields are deliberately excluded from the template and modelled only so that they can be rejected with an actionable message:

Scheduler placement versus the emitted static workload. Fields such as nodeSelector, affinity, tolerations and topologySpreadConstraints decide which node the scheduling probe is scheduled onto. kubelet never schedules a static Pod: it starts whatever file it finds, on the node whose kubelet finds it. Placement therefore belongs to spec.placement of the StaticSet, and the operator strips those fields from the emitted static Pod. A template that sets them is rejected rather than accepted and ignored.

API-dependent references. serviceAccountName, automountServiceAccountToken, imagePullSecrets, schedulerName, priorityClassName and enableServiceLinks all require a live API server or a scheduler, so they cannot survive an offline host reboot and are rejected.

The models here are therefore not the official client's V1Pod family, even though those are pydantic models too. They are the StaticSet API: they define the CRD, they forbid unknown fields, and they name the alternative when a field cannot be honoured. Using V1Pod would admit every field Kubernetes has, including the ones this operator must refuse, and would turn a rejection into a silent drop. The official models are used for the scheduler-placement API and where objects cross the API boundary — see :mod:static_sets.models and :mod:static_sets.api.

(str | None, default: None ) –

The RuntimeClass the static Pod is started with.

Passed through to the manifest because a workload may legitimately need a non-default runtime (a sandboxed or a GPU runtime). Note what it costs: kubelet resolves a RuntimeClass through its own cache of the API object, so a workload that declares one is not guaranteed to start on a host reboot that happens while the API server is unreachable. Leave it unset for a workload whose whole point is to come back disconnected.

The scheduling probe cannot use it — the probe must never start — so it is carried on the probe's staticsets.cloudlane.dev/runtime-class label and applied when the manifest is rendered.

The limit is 63 characters because the value doubles as a label value; a RuntimeClass name is a DNS subdomain, which longer names would also be.

docs.title: The StaticSet reference
docs.text:
apiVersion: staticsets.cloudlane.dev/v1
kind: StaticSet
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: static-sets
spec: {…}
status: {…}

Namespaced, plural staticsets, singular staticset, short name sset, served and stored as v1. The CRD is generated from the Pydantic models (uv run app/render_crds.py) and installed by the chart from crds/.

docs.title: spec
docs.text:
Field Type Default Meaning mode Deployment | DaemonSet — How many placements the scheduler is asked for, and by what kind of probe. replicas integer 0–64 — Desired placements. Required for Deployment, invalid for DaemonSet. template PodTemplateSpec — The workload. Restricted to the supported subset. placement Placement {} Scheduler placement for the scheduling probe, and therefore for the workload. update UpdatePolicy see below How a new revision replaces an old placement. offline OfflinePolicy see below What must hold before a revision may be published. cleanup CleanupPolicy see below How unwanted placements are removed. policy WorkloadPolicy see below Guards on the static workload itself.

There is no installer field: where a static Pod is written is a property of the node, not of a StaticSet. The chart configures the manager once per node (manager.staticPodPath, manager.bundleDir), which is what stops a StaticSet from widening the host access of the process that writes it.

docs.title: spec.placement
docs.text:
Steers the Kubernetes scheduler, which places the scheduling probe's Pods. Copied onto the probe, never onto the emitted static Pod; see placement and capacity.

Field Meaning nodeSelector Label equality requirements. affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution Required node selector terms (matchExpressions, matchFields). affinity.nodeAffinity.preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution Weighted preferred terms. tolerations Tolerations the workload's placement requires. topologySpreadConstraints The upstream V1TopologySpreadConstraint: maxSkew, topologyKey, whenUnsatisfiable (default DoNotSchedule), labelSelector, minDomains, and the pass-through matchLabelKeys/nodeAffinityPolicy/nodeTaintsPolicy.

The field types are the generated Kubernetes client models, so the CRD documents the scheduler API as Kubernetes defines it. The operator still refuses what it cannot act on, with the field named: pod affinity and anti-affinity, node-selector and label-selector operators outside the set it evaluates, toleration operators/effects outside the API server's set, and a preferred-term weight outside 1–100.

docs.title: spec.update
docs.text: Field Default Meaning strategy Recreate Recreate retires the old placement before installing the new one; Surge installs the new one first. maxSurge 0 Placements that may overlap under Surge. Must be 0 under Recreate. maxUnavailable 0 Installer replicas that may be unavailable during a Surge rollout. Ignored under Recreate. gracePeriodSeconds 300 Reserved. Accepted and validated, but not yet used to bound retirement.

docs.title: spec.offline
docs.text: Field Default Meaning retainedRevisions 2 Revision directories kept per placement, newest first. The active revision is always kept. imageProvisioning ExternallyProvisioned ExternallyProvisioned means image availability is someone else's problem, and status says so. VerifiedBeforeInstall refuses to publish a revision until a checker confirms the images are present. allowDisconnectedStart true Whether imagePullPolicy: Always is accepted. Set to false to require IfNotPresent or Never everywhere.

docs.title: spec.cleanup
docs.text: Field Default Meaning onNodeUnreachable Retain Retain keeps a cleanup intent pending and keeps reporting it. AbandonAfterGrace lets an administrator stop waiting after abandonmentGraceSeconds, without ever claiming the remote workload was removed. abandonmentGraceSeconds 3600 The grace period AbandonAfterGrace refers to. removeConfigurationAfterAck true Whether the materialized configuration is deleted once cleanup is acknowledged.

docs.title: spec.policy
docs.text: Field Default Meaning allowPrivileged false Permit securityContext.privileged in the workload. A static Pod is started by kubelet straight from a file, so nothing else reviews it. allowInlineSecretEnv false Permit Secret material to be written into the static Pod manifest as an environment value. See Secret handling.

docs.title: spec.template.spec.runtimeClassName
docs.text: Optional, and passed through to the static Pod's manifest. It is the one API-adjacent Pod field a static Pod can keep, because kubelet resolves it through its own cache rather than through a scheduler. Note the cost: a RuntimeClass is an API object, so a workload that declares one is not guaranteed to start on a reboot that happens while the API server is unreachable. Leave it unset for a workload whose point is to come back disconnected. The value must fit a label value (≤63 characters), because it is also carried on the scheduling probe's staticsets.cloudlane.dev/runtime-class label — the probe itself must run under a placeholder class that no node can start.

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Field Meaning observedGeneration The metadata.generation this status describes. placedGeneration The generation a complete scheduling pass has been carried out for. A pass is only started when this lags behind, when a placement is missing, or when a new eligible node appears. desiredRevision The revision every installed placement agrees on, or unset while a rollout has two revisions in flight — revisions are content hashes, so there is no honest "newest" to report. placements[] What each node's manager did: identity, node, revision, phase (Pending, Installing, Installed, Retiring, Cleaning, Cleaned, Failed), acknowledged, generation, message. health[] What was observed: identity, node, observed, phase, ready, restartCount, message, derived from the mirror Pods. cleanup[] Each cleanup intent: identity, node, revision, generation, reason, state (Requested, Acknowledged, Blocked, Abandoned), acknowledged, message. conditions[] Standard Kubernetes conditions, listed below.

Installed state is deliberately separate from observed health. A placement can be Installed and unhealthy, or Installed and unobservable because its node is gone; neither is a reason to reinstall.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text: Type Status Reason Meaning Synchronized True when the operator's view of the cluster is complete; False with reason Synchronizing before that. Synchronized, Synchronizing Until this is True the operator performs no destructive action. Ready True when every desired placement is installed, acknowledged and mirrored. AllPlacementsInstalled, PlacementsPending, Deleting CleanupPending True while any cleanup intent is unacknowledged. CleanupPending, CleanupComplete Scheduling True while a scheduling pass is in progress. ProbeCreated, ProbePending, Unschedulable, Installing, RetiringPreviousPlacement, Placed Degraded True when a placement reported a failure. PlacementFailed Deleting True while a deleted StaticSet is cleaning up. ResourceDeleted CleanedUp True once every placement acknowledged removal. The finalizer is released at that point. CleanupAcknowledged, CleanupPending

docs.title: Example
docs.text: See deploy/samples/: deployment-mode.yaml, daemonset-mode.yaml, secret-volume.yaml and the configmap.yaml they reference. The sample set is validated by the test suite, so it always describes objects the operator accepts.

docs.title: Translation: the supported workload subset
docs.text:
A static Pod is started by kubelet directly from a file, so none of the machinery that normally resolves a Pod's references runs for it: there is no admission controller, no scheduler, and — after the reboot this exists for — no API server. The operator therefore compiles the template into a self-contained Pod: every reference is resolved at install time, every piece of configuration is materialized on the node, and anything it cannot resolve that way is rejected.

Rejection is the point. A template field that was silently dropped would produce a Pod that starts, looks healthy, and behaves differently from what was asked for.

docs.title: What the emitted Pod contains
docs.text:
Kind Fields Pod containers, initContainers, volumes, restartPolicy (always Always), terminationGracePeriodSeconds, dnsPolicy, dnsConfig, hostNetwork, hostPID, hostIPC, hostname, hostAliases, shareProcessNamespace, securityContext Container name, image, imagePullPolicy, command, args, workingDir, env, envFrom, ports, resources, volumeMounts, livenessProbe, readinessProbe, startupProbe, securityContext, stdin, stdinOnce, tty Probe exec, httpGet, tcpSocket, grpc, and the timing and threshold fields Volume configMap, secret, emptyDir Volume mount name, mountPath, readOnly Template metadata labels, annotations

Everything else is refused. A field the model does not know is rejected by validation; a field the model knows but the compiler cannot honour is rejected with a message that names it and, where one exists, the alternative.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Environment values are resolved to literals at install time, because a static Pod cannot resolve a configMapKeyRef or a secretKeyRef offline: kubelet would have to ask the API server.

  • env[].value is kept as-is.
  • env[].valueFrom.configMapKeyRef is resolved from the ConfigMap now. A missing key fails unless optional: true, in which case the variable is omitted.
  • envFrom[].configMapRef expands every key, applying prefix. Sources are applied in order, so a later source wins over an earlier one; explicit env entries are applied last and win over everything, matching Kubernetes' own precedence.
  • Keys that are not valid environment variable names are dropped, as Kubernetes does.
  • A value that is not valid UTF-8 text cannot become an environment variable; it is refused with a message that suggests mounting it as a file instead.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
A ConfigMap value is not confidential, so inlining it is safe. A Secret value is not, and a static Pod has no offline way to resolve one:

  • as a volume — supported, and the recommended shape. The data is materialized as a file inside the revision directory with a restrictive mode, and the emitted Pod mounts that directory read-only. The value never appears in the manifest, in the mirror Pod, or in status.
  • as an environment value — refused unless spec.policy.allowInlineSecretEnv is true. The only offline ways to satisfy the request both disclose the value: either it is written into the manifest, where the mirror Pod and every copy of the file expose it, or the variable is simply gone after the reboot. With the opt-in the value is inlined and the disclosure is recorded in the placement's warnings so it is visible in status.

docs.title: Secret volume modes
docs.text:
Secret files are written with mode 0400 by default — the most restrictive mode that still works when the container runs as root. When the container is not provably root (the template declares a non-root user, or declares nothing at all), that file would be unreadable, so the template must state volumes[].secret.defaultMode explicitly. This is refused rather than guessed at:

container 'web' mounts Secret volume 'tls' without a defaultMode; the manager writes
Secret files as 0400, which a non-root container cannot read. Set
spec.template.spec.volumes[].secret.defaultMode explicitly, or declare the container as
root with securityContext.runAsUser: 0

docs.title: Volumes
docs.text:
Source Handling configMap Materialized as files under the revision directory (0644 by default), mounted read-only as a hostPath. items selects keys, renames them and sets per-file modes; optional makes an absent ConfigMap or key acceptable. secret As above, under a secrets/ directory, with 0400 as the default mode. emptyDir Passed through unchanged: kubelet provides it without the API server. hostPath Refused. The only hostPath mounts in the manifest are the revision directories the operator materialized, which keeps the workload inside the bundle the manager owns. persistentVolumeClaim Refused. Attaching a volume needs the API server and a bound PV. projected, downwardAPI, nfs, … Refused. Each needs a source that will not exist offline.

volumeMounts[].subPath, subPathExpr, mountPropagation and recursiveReadOnly are refused: they change path semantics against a volume the manager owns, and a sub-path would escape the directory that was validated.

Item paths are validated, so an item cannot map a key outside its own volume directory.

docs.title: Probes, resources and security contexts
docs.text:
Probes, resources, container and Pod securityContext and ports are preserved unchanged. A probe that declares no handler is refused, because kubelet would reject the Pod anyway and the error would be harder to read.

securityContext.privileged: true is refused unless spec.policy.allowPrivileged is set: kubelet starts a static Pod straight from a file, so no admission controller gets a chance to review it.

docs.title: What the emitted Pod deliberately does not carry
docs.text:
Scheduler placement. nodeSelector, affinity, tolerations and topologySpreadConstraints in the template are rejected with a message pointing at spec.placement. kubelet never schedules a static Pod, so those fields would be inert, and silently deleting them would look like they had been honoured.

API-dependent references. These are refused because a static Pod must survive a reboot with no API server:

Field Why serviceAccountName, automountServiceAccountToken A projected service-account token is fetched from the API server; without one, a client that needs credentials cannot start. imagePullSecrets Pull credentials come from a Secret through the API server. Pre-pull the image and use IfNotPresent. schedulerName There is no scheduler. priorityClassName Admission resolves it; kubelet cannot preempt for a static Pod. enableServiceLinks Service environment variables are discovered from the API server.

docs.title: Revisions
docs.text:
The revision is a hash of the compiled Pod (with relative configuration paths, so it does not depend on where the bundle is mounted) and of every materialized file and its mode. Two consequences matter:

  • it is deterministic: the same template and the same resolved configuration always produce the same revision, so a reconcile that changes nothing is not a rollout;
  • it is content-sensitive: editing a referenced ConfigMap or Secret produces a new revision, because the file content is part of the hash.

Nothing node-specific enters the hash, so all placements of a StaticSet agree on what desiredRevision means.

docs.title: The admission caveat
docs.text: The generated CRD is a structural schema, so the API server prunes a field it does not know instead of refusing it. Without the validating webhook (webhook.enabled=true in the chart, which needs cert-manager) an unknown template field is dropped by the API server before the operator ever sees it — the one case where "never silently dropped" degrades to "dropped by somebody else". Deploy with the webhook enabled if that matters to you; see How to install.
